description: A browser-based tamagotchi game where you care for a skateboard that degrades over time and can snap in two if neglected

userStories.title: Project scaffolding and game loop
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the project scaffolded with Bun + TypeScript and a working game loop so that subsequent stories have a foundation to build on
acceptanceCriteria: package.json exists with bun as runtime and typescript as dependency
tsconfig.json configured for ES2022 target with strict mode enabled
src/index.ts entry point exists and runs without errors via `bun run src/index.ts`
Game class in src/game/Game.ts implements a requestAnimationFrame-based game loop
Game loop exposes start(), stop(), and tick(deltaTime) methods
public/index.html contains a <canvas> element with id 'game-canvas' sized 800x600
bun run type-check passes with zero errors
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Greenfield project. Initialize with `bun init`. Install typescript: `bun add --dev typescript @types/node`. Configure tsconfig.json for module: ESNext, target: ES2022, strict: true. Game loop should track last timestamp and calculate deltaTime each frame.
userStories.notes: Completed with 51 tests. Game class uses RAF loop with delta clamping.

userStories.title: Core types and game state management
userStories.description: As a developer, I want core type definitions and a GameState manager so that all game systems share a single source of truth
acceptanceCriteria: src/types/game-types.ts defines BoardStats interface with deckIntegrity, wheelWear, truckTightness, gripCondition (all number 0-100)
src/types/game-types.ts defines GamePhase type as union: 'new' | 'playing' | 'warning' | 'critical' | 'snapped' | 'paused'
src/types/game-types.ts defines GameState interface with stats, phase, score, ticksAlive, lastTick fields
src/types/game-types.ts defines CareAction interface with id, label, shortcut, cooldown, lastUsed, effects fields
src/game/GameState.ts exports a GameState class that initializes all stats to 100 on construction
GameState.update(deltaTime) method advances ticksAlive and returns updated state
GameState.reset() restores all stats to 100 and phase to 'new'
Type-check passes with zero errors
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Create src/types/ directory. Use TypeScript interfaces exclusively (no classes for data types). GameState should be a class with private state and public methods. Follow the type definitions from prd.md Technical Context section.
userStories.notes: Completed with 84 tests across 2 test files (131 total project tests). GameState uses setOnTick callback hook for external degradation systems.

userStories.title: Stat degradation system
userStories.description: As a player, I want my skateboard's stats to degrade over time so that I must actively maintain it
acceptanceCriteria: src/systems/degradation.ts exports a degradeStats(stats, deltaTime) function
Each stat degrades at a configurable rate per second (defined in src/game/constants.ts)
Base degradation rates: deckIntegrity 0.5%/sec, wheelWear 1.2%/sec, truckTightness 0.8%/sec, gripCondition 1.0%/sec
Interconnected effects: if truckTightness < 30, deckIntegrity degrades 2x faster; if gripCondition < 30, deckIntegrity degrades 1.5x faster
Stats floor at 0 (never go negative)
Game phase auto-updates: 'warning' when any stat < 30, 'critical' when any stat < 10
src/game/constants.ts exports all degradation rates as a DegradationConfig object
Type-check passes with zero errors
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Create src/systems/ and src/game/ directories. degradation.ts should be pure functions taking stats and deltaTime, returning new stats. Use constants.ts for all magic numbers. Test interconnected effects with edge cases (both truckTightness and gripCondition below 30).
userStories.notes: Completed with 48 tests. Pure function degradation system with interconnected effects and phase auto-updates. Constants centralized in DegradationConfig.

userStories.title: Skateboard canvas rendering
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see my skateboard rendered on screen so that I can visually track its condition
acceptanceCriteria: src/render/board-renderer.ts exports a renderBoard(ctx, stats) function
Skateboard drawn as a top-down view: rectangular deck (brown wood color), grip tape strip (black), trucks (gray rectangles), wheels (white circles)
Board centered on canvas at coordinates calculated from canvas width/height
Board dimensions: deck 120px wide x 320px tall, wheels 24px diameter, trucks 60px wide
renderBoard accepts BoardStats and adjusts visual appearance based on stats (color shifts toward damaged look as stats drop)
Wheel color darkens as wheelWear decreases; deck browns/darkens as deckIntegrity decreases
src/render/board-renderer.ts exports a CANVAS_WIDTH and CANVAS_HEIGHT constant matching index.html canvas size
Type-check passes with zero errors
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Use Canvas2DContext API. Board should be drawn with ctx.fillRect, ctx.arc, ctx.beginPath etc. No external rendering libraries. Keep draw functions pure — accept ctx and data, produce side effects on canvas only. Test by verifying functions execute without throwing given a mock CanvasRenderingContext2D.

userStories.title: Care action system with cooldowns
userStories.description: As a player, I want to perform care actions on my skateboard so that I can restore its stats and prevent damage
acceptanceCriteria: src/systems/care-actions.ts exports an array of CareAction objects: 'tighten-trucks', 'replace-wheels', 'sand-grip-tape', 'apply-wax'
Each action restores specific stats: tighten-trucks (+25 truckTightness), replace-wheels (+30 wheelWear), sand-grip-tape (+25 gripCondition), apply-wax (+15 all stats)
Each action has a cooldown: tighten-trucks 8s, replace-wheels 15s, sand-grip-tape 10s, apply-wax 20s
canPerformAction(actionId, actions, currentTime) returns false if action is on cooldown
performAction(actionId, state, currentTime) applies stat effects (capped at 100), updates lastUsed, increments score by 10
apply-wax has no shortcut key initially (reserved for future expansion)
Type-check passes with zero errors
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Care actions defined as const array of CareAction objects. performAction should be a pure function: takes state + actionId + timestamp, returns new state. Cooldowns tracked via lastUsed timestamp on each action. Stats capped at 100 using Math.min.

userStories.title: Status bar UI overlay
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see visual status bars for each stat so that I can quickly assess my board's condition
acceptanceCriteria: src/render/ui-renderer.ts exports renderStatusBar(ctx, stats) function
Four horizontal bars rendered at top of canvas: Deck Integrity, Wheel Wear, Truck Tightness, Grip Condition
Each bar shows label text and a filled rectangle proportional to stat value (0-100%)
Bar colors: green when stat > 60%, orange when 30-60%, red when < 30%
Score displayed as text in top-right corner
Care action buttons rendered as labeled rectangles below the status bars
Buttons show cooldown timer (remaining seconds) when on cooldown, dimmed appearance
Type-check passes with zero errors
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Use Canvas2DContext for all UI rendering — no DOM overlay. renderStatusBar draws filled rectangles for bars, ctx.fillText for labels. Button hit regions tracked as an array of {id, x, y, w, h} objects returned by renderButtons() for click detection. Color interpolation: green(0,180,0) → orange(255,165,0) → red(220,40,40).

userStories.title: Damage visuals (cracks and degradation)
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see my skateboard visually crack and degrade so that the threat of snapping feels real
acceptanceCriteria: src/systems/damage-visuals.ts exports generateCracks(deckIntegrity) returning an array of Crack objects
Crack object has: startX, startY, points[] (array of {x, y}), severity (0-1)
When deckIntegrity > 70: no cracks rendered
When deckIntegrity 40-70: 1-2 hairline cracks appear randomly on deck
When deckIntegrity 20-40: 3-5 cracks, thicker lines, some branching
When deckIntegrity < 20: 6+ cracks spanning most of the deck, one major crack forming a split line
renderCracks(ctx, cracks) draws cracks as jagged black/dark brown lines on canvas
Crack positions are seeded by ticksAlive so they're deterministic per game session
Type-check passes with zero errors
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Use a simple seeded PRNG (mulberry32 or similar) for deterministic crack generation. Cracks generated as arrays of line segments. renderCracks uses ctx.beginPath/lineTo/stroke with variable line width based on severity. Seed should be derived from game start timestamp so cracks are consistent within a session but different across sessions.

userStories.title: Board snap animation and game over screen
userStories.description: As a player, I want a dramatic snap animation when my board breaks so that the stakes feel meaningful and I'm motivated to try again
acceptanceCriteria: Game transitions to 'snapped' phase when deckIntegrity reaches 0
Snap animation plays over ~2 seconds: board splits along the major crack line, two halves separate with slight rotation
src/render/effects.ts exports renderSnapAnimation(ctx, progress) where progress is 0-1
At progress 0: board intact; at progress 0.5: crack widens and halves start separating; at progress 1.0: halves fully separated
After animation completes, game over screen renders: 'YOUR BOARD SNAPPED' text, final score, time survived
'Play Again' button rendered on canvas — clicking it resets the game to a fresh board
src/render/effects.ts exports renderGameOver(ctx, score, ticksAlive) function
Type-check passes with zero errors
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Snap animation: split the deck drawing into two halves at the major crack line. Use ctx.save/restore and ctx.translate/ctx.rotate to animate separation. Game over text centered on canvas with large font. Play Again button is a styled rectangle — click detection handled by US-009's click system. Animate using requestAnimationFrame with easing (ease-in for dramatic effect).

userStories.title: Keyboard input for care actions
userStories.description: As a player, I want to use keyboard shortcuts to perform care actions so that I can react quickly when stats are dropping
acceptanceCriteria: src/input/keyboard.ts exports setupKeyboard(canvas, onAction) function that adds keydown listener
Key bindings: '1' = tighten-trucks, '2' = replace-wheels, '3' = sand-grip-tape, '4' = apply-wax
Pressing a bound key triggers the corresponding care action via onAction callback with actionId
Pressing 'p' or 'Escape' toggles game pause/unpause
Input only processes when game phase is 'playing' (not during snapped, new, or paused)
Keyboard events are preventDefault'd to avoid browser shortcuts interfering
src/input/click.ts exports setupClick(canvas, buttons, onClick) for mouse click detection on UI buttons
Type-check passes with zero errors
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: keyboard.ts: addEventListener('keydown', ...) on canvas element. Map key codes to action IDs. Pass callback pattern — don't import GameState directly (keep input layer decoupled). click.ts: addEventListener('click', ...), check if click coordinates fall within any button hit region returned by renderButtons(). Both use functional callbacks for testability.

userStories.title: localStorage persistence (save/load)
userStories.description: As a player, I want my game to save automatically so that I don't lose progress if I close the browser
acceptanceCriteria: src/persistence/save-load.ts exports saveGame(state) and loadGame() functions
saveGame serializes GameState to JSON and stores in localStorage under key 'skateboard-tamagotchi-save'
loadGame reads from localStorage, parses JSON, returns GameState or null if no save exists
Game auto-saves every 10 seconds during playing phase (timer in Game.ts)
On game initialization, loadGame is called — if save exists, state is restored; otherwise fresh board
Saved state includes: stats, score, ticksAlive, cracks seed; excludes lastTick (reset on load)
localStorage errors (quota exceeded, disabled) are caught and logged without crashing
Type-check passes with zero errors
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Use try/catch around localStorage.get/setItem. saveGame should serialize a copy of state (not the live object). On load, validate that returned data has expected fields before applying. Auto-save timer: track elapsed time in game loop, trigger save every 10000ms. For testing, mock localStorage with a simple in-memory Map.
